result.title: Where Does Free-Text 3D Grounding Fail? An Error Analysis of Report-Sentence Segmentation in Chest CT
result.summary: Free-text 3D grounding, segmenting in a CT volume the region described by one sentence of the radiology report, could link reports to images at scale, but it is unclear where current models fail. We analyse the publicly released VoxTell model on all 381 findings of the 200-scan ReXGroundingCT validation set, where it grounds 53.5% of findings. Its failures are rarely about which lesion or side is meant. No miss lies on the side opposite to the one named, and findings are almost never confused with one another. Instead, predictions are too large, land on a neighbouring lesion on the correct side, or are missing for small findings, and diffuse findings are rarely grounded. Removing location words halves performance, to the level of label-only prompting, and anatomical rules derived from the sentence never improve the full-sentence output. The same pattern holds on the hidden 300-scan test set. Further progress therefore depends on extent estimation and small-lesion sensitivity rather than on anatomical post-processing.

AI.brief_summary: 对已公开的 VoxTell 模型在 ReXGroundingCT 胸部 CT 验证集全部 381 条发现上做逐例错误分析，发现失败主要不在病灶或左右侧的选择，而在范围估计过大、落到同侧邻近病灶、小结节漏检和弥漫性病变难以定位。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接关乎视觉证据是否被真正使用：去掉位置词后性能减半至仅用标签的水平，且句法推出的解剖规则无增益，可供核查 LVR 中空间与范围信息的表示、视觉旁路与证据筛选问题。
